primitives.name: Kick-Out Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: (c) A Kick-out is a drop-kick, place-kick or punt made by a player of the side which has made a safety or a touchback.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K': 'kick type (dimensionless)', 'S': 'side making safety or touchback (dimensionless)', 'P': 'player executing kick (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Kick-out occurs only after safety or touchback; kick is executed by defending side.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ball is dead or called down before return to field.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a controlled stochastic process where K ∈ {drop, place, punt} and S determines initial field state.
layer2.telemetry: Ball trajectory, field position, and outcome classification

primitives.name: Free-Kick Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: (f) A Frce-kick is a term used to designate any kick when the opponents are restrained by rule from advancing beyond a certain point before the ball is put in play.
primitives.assumptions: Opponents must remain behind a defined line until ball is in play.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When rule enforcement restricts opponent movement prior to kick.

layer2.mapping: Kernel of constraint-based motion where O defines a temporal and spatial boundary for opponent behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Opponent positioning relative to line of scrimmage

primitives.name: Boundary Condition
primitives.verbatim_quote: (a) The ball is Out of Bounds when it touches the ground on or outside the side line or side line extended, or when any part of the player who hplds the ball touches the ground on or outside the side line or side line extended.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B': 'ball position vector (meters)', 'L': 'side line coordinate (meters)', 'P': 'player contact point (meters)'}
primitives.assumptions: Ball or player contact with boundary triggers out-of-bounds condition.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B or P exceeds L in either direction.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a geometric boundary function where B ∈ ℝ² and L defines a hyperplane.
